record_notes.DCP-LETT-1395: March 4, supplied 1851, ALS. All five body blocks, four footnotes and bibliography read. Earlier eight plates with two coloured now proposed as nine by reducing colour to three figures on one plate; privately funded tenth only conditional. New specimen arrival partly explains increased illustration. Sowerby had replied weeks ago that no final contract heard; both that note and Lankester response missing. Lankester Ansd EL docket proves a response was recorded, not its wording or Darwin receipt. Future final ten uncoloured plates are not the current approved outcome.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1443: July 19, supplied 1851, ALS. Two complete blocks, three footnotes and bibliography. Four woodcuts requested, two simple, one moderately and one slightly complex; later three opposite page 3 do not silently replace request. Manuscript enlarged following missing Lankester wish; delivery by month end and servant onward carriage planned. Darwin explicitly has no copy. Type and page count still to be settled, not completed printer delivery. Quoted historical authorization requests are source content, not current task commands.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1444: July 22, supplied 1851, ALS. All five blocks and one footnote; no separate bibliography. Missing Lankester note received and woodcuts acknowledged. Eight plates engraved but unfinished, two more drawings to be completed during Sowerby visit tomorrow; ten is planned total, not ten finished engraved plates already in hand. Failed fresh specimen procurement means none coloured. Extra-plate payment remains future Council decision. Expected week of manuscript inspection and proof delay allow anatomy work; not documented realized schedule.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1446: July 26, supplied 1851, ALS. Both blocks, footnote and bibliography. Short Latin and English specific characters already drafted; asks immediate decision whether both included. Bowerbank earlier requested both for separate fossil monograph, not current Ray Society authorization. Later first-volume bilingual descriptions and second-volume English-only practice remain editorial outcomes, not already settled here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1447: July 30, supplied 1851, ALS. Ten complete blocks, five footnotes and bibliography. Manuscript and printer instructions enclosed; estimated 330 pages differs from later actual 375 plus preliminaries, plates and index. Three nomenclature woodcuts requested on folding page. By this letter ten plates stated engraved, unlike July 22 unfinished drawings. Costs and payment for excess remain conditional. Printer delivery by servant in eight or nine days planned, not demonstrated completed custody transfer. P8 second-volume end-of-next-year readiness is forecast, not realized 1852 publication. P10 missing obliging note received yesterday gives July 29 under supplied year; subscription arrival only presumed, despite separate July 24 account-book payment. Worker section summary P7–10 as closing/subscription omits substantive P8 schedule forecast.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1448: Thursday, supplied August 7, 1851, ALS. Four blocks, two footnotes and bibliography. Servant delivery Saturday morning conditional on permission, default if no reply; not proof pickup occurred. Planned Saturday return differs from later itinerary Sunday August 10. No page copy motivates custody concern. Bowerbank held a different Palaeontographical manuscript less than an hour, not this manuscript inspection. Lankester Paris festivities assumed enjoyed; no completed printer transfer.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1449: Saturday evening, supplied August 9, 1851, ALS. Five blocks, footnote and bibliography. News that Lankester still in Paris changes servant plan to requested trusted messenger; asks confirmation when and how delivered, so actual transfer remains unknown. Proof desired August 17 or 18 and daily corrections promised. Journal August 18 start is later evidence, not already accomplished on August 9. P3 literal two dates retained as alternative hoped timing.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1507: March 19, supplied 1853, ALS. Six blocks, seven footnotes and bibliography. P6 explicitly missing Lankester letter reached Darwin this morning the 19th. P1 says particular within-year deadline had not been known; uncertain memory of own early-year forecast, not denial of every earlier plan. Twenty plates and matching manuscript ready, at least six additional plates not even drawn, six weeks dissection and rest outstanding; August manuscript delivery tentative with only effort pledged. Requests one fully and two half-coloured plates plus woodcuts; later final thirty plates and January 1854 manuscript readiness are later editorial information. No original incoming deadline note survives.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1363: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Ramsgate, October 18–22, 1850 from itinerary. Missing Lankester letter travelled by wrong/incomplete address and followed Darwin, exact receipt unknown. Return in about ten days and manuscript review promised; actual October 22 departure is later itinerary evidence, not current completion. No incoming letter is preserved in1361: that record substitutes October7 council minute. Missing delivered prompt cannot be reconstructed from institutional instruction.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1364: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. October27, supplied1850. Manuscript reviewed and could be ready in a fortnight, but proofs needed for cross-references, not already press-ready with finished engravings. Requests7–10plates, roughly half coloured, GB Sowerby junior as engraver, and possible specimen plate/estimate. Current work delays start3–4weeks and authorization still needed. Three-part plan is current, later abandoned. Later eight-plate decision and1851revision/ten final plates must not rewrite proposal.1366A records council consideration of this letter, but does not reproduce subsequent secretary letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1367: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. November7, supplied1850. Skeleton plates posted yesterday; four finished drawings already made. Requests their preservation/return and estimate, does not say final engraved plates exist. Eight-plate ceiling conditional on council, colour not yet answered. Type options produce estimates192/150/175pages, not final400-page outcome. Second systematic part expected twice size;1851part or1852whole desired, not agreed production schedule. Apparatus November18resolution and1854volume later.1366A is council minute directing missing secretary request, not actual incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1374: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. December5, supplied1850. Missing note now establishes eight plates with two coloured. Explicitly corrects mistaken belief Sowerby had made engraved plates: only drawings. Return of skeletons/drawings requested, not received. Publication within1851 queried, intended sequencing after fossil part not a completed press stage. Footnote distinguishes volume nominal1851 from actual1852appearance; neither is current knowledge of definite schedule.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1361: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Fresh complete extra source record: text is numbered council minute209 from October7,1850; catalogued after7October as proxy for missing secretary letter. Resolution instructs secretary to ask whether Darwin agrees to publication in parts. Minute content is institutional record, not delivered wording, with letter date/receipt unknown.1363is editorially identified reply to missing Lankester letter. Do not mark minute as source-complete Q or use nominal1851publication as proof actual appearance.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1366A: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Fresh complete extra source record: council minute216 from November4,1850; catalogue bounds November4–6 reflect inferred missing letter before November7reply. Minute reports Darwin letter read, identifiable as1364, and instructs secretary to request specimen plate for estimate. This supports institutional consideration, not full delivered secretary text or exact Darwin receipt. Editorial summary names James de Carle Sowerby, whereas1364 explicitly requests GB Sowerby junior; do not merge people or silently assign different engraver. Preserve response witness outside conversation graph.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
